title: Component formula for the Weil action on a constant-extension image
statement:
Fix $q=p^a$, $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, and $\Qlb=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. Let $X_0$ be a separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme, $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, $m\ge1$, $k_m=\mathbf F_{q^m}\subset k$, and $g:X_{0,m}=X_0\times_{k_0}k_m\to X_0$. Let $\mathcal F=(M,\theta)$ be a constructible $\Qlb$-Weil sheaf [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex], with $\theta:G_X^*M\xrightarrow{\sim}M$ for geometric $q$-Frobenius. Form $P=g_*g^*\mathcal F$ using [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom, def-weil-derived-direct-image] and the canonical induced Weil structures of [lem-fix-weil-operations].
Index the clopen sheets of $Y=X_{0,m}\times_{k_0}k$ by $I=\operatorname{Hom}_{k_0}(k_m,k)$, using the projection identifications with $X$ (on affine coordinates $a\otimes b\mapsto a\sigma(b)$). Let $G_Y$ be geometric $q$-Frobenius on $Y$ [def-weil-frobenius-detailed]; since $g$ is a $k_0$-morphism, the projection $h:Y\to X$ satisfies $hG_Y=G_Xh$, so $G_Y$ maps each sheet $Y_\sigma$ into a sheet $Y_{\pi(\sigma)}$, and in the sheet identifications $G_Y|_{Y_\sigma}$ is $G_X$. This defines the permutation $\pi:I\to I$. Under the natural underlying-heart identification $P\simeq\bigoplus_{\sigma\in I}M$ of [lem-zl-split-sheet-adjunction], its induced Weil map is the componentwise map $\theta$ followed by this permutation:
$$\theta_P((v_\sigma)_\sigma)=(\theta(v_{\pi(\sigma)}))_\sigma,$$
where $v_\sigma$ lies in the $\sigma$-component $G_X^*M$ of $G_X^*P$; the Frobenius exchange $G_X^*h_*\simeq h_*G_Y^*$ places the $\pi(\sigma)$-component of $G_X^*P$ on the sheet $Y_\sigma$.
This formula denotes equality of morphisms in the clopen product category, with source components $G_X^*M$, and not merely equality on stalks. It is compatible with finite coefficient extension and with the canonical Frobenius exchange for the actual derived operations. The adjunction unit corresponds to the equivariant diagonal $M\to\bigoplus_\sigma M$. No lissity, connectedness or semisimplicity hypothesis is required.

proof.text:
Write $P_X=LG_X^*$ and $P_Y=LG_Y^*$. The geometric decomposition in clause (b) of [lem-zl-constant-extension-weil-heart-equivalence] supplies the finite clopen sheets. Fix their projection sections $s_\sigma:X\to Y$ as in the statement. Put $\gamma=\varphi_q^{-1}$, as in [def-weil-frobenius-detailed]. In an affine chart write
$$r_\sigma:A_0\otimes_{k_0}k_m\otimes_{k_0}k\to A_0\otimes_{k_0}k,\quad a\otimes b\otimes c\mapsto a\otimes\sigma(b)c.$$
The definition of $G_Y$ gives
$$r_\sigma G_Y^\#=G_X^\#r_{\varphi_q\sigma},$$
because $\gamma(\varphi_q\sigma(b))=\sigma(b)$. Hence $G_Ys_\sigma=s_{\pi(\sigma)}G_X$ with $\pi(\sigma)=\varphi_q\circ\sigma$. This is a permutation, with inverse $\gamma\circ\sigma$. The formula uses the labelled field embeddings and therefore specifies $\pi$ also when $X$ is empty. The equations agree on overlaps, since each $s_\sigma$ is the prescribed global projection section.

source.place: Paragraph 5: the permutation of the copies, with its direction checked in the projection coordinates

proof.text:
By [lem-zl-split-sheet-adjunction], in the clopen coordinates $H_\sigma=s_\sigma^*H$ the actual functors are
$$Lh^*K=(K)_\sigma,\qquad Rh_*H=\prod_\sigma H_\sigma,$$
with diagonal unit and counit $\varepsilon_{H,\sigma}=\operatorname{pr}_\sigma$. In particular $Rh_*Lh^*M=\bigoplus_\sigma M$ in the heart. The exact Frobenius equivalences of [lem-pod-semilinear-field-operation-lifts] preserve finite products: apply their inverse to a product cone and its universal property. Thus the source coordinates of $P_XRh_*H$ are $P_XH_\tau$. Step 1 gives $(P_YH)_\sigma=P_XH_{\pi(\sigma)}$: the identification is $s_\sigma^*G_Y^*\simeq(G_Ys_\sigma)^*=(s_{\pi(\sigma)}G_X)^*\simeq G_X^*s_{\pi(\sigma)}^*$, built from the integral composition isomorphisms $c_{h,k}$ of [lem-pod-integral-pullback-composition] at the finite stage $E$ over which $M$ is represented, rationalized as in the definition of the field-coefficient pullbacks.

source.place: Paragraph 5: the actual direct-image and adjunction coordinates before the Frobenius comparison

proof.text:
Compute the prescribed exchange $e_H:P_XRh_*H\to Rh_*P_YH$ as a mate, not as a chosen isomorphism between products. The commuting Frobenius square is Cartesian, since its horizontal arrows are automorphisms. For the $k$-scheme convention of [fix-lem-exchanges], give its source corners structural maps $a_XG_X$ and $a_YG_Y$; they remain finite-type $k$-schemes and $h$ remains a $k$-morphism. Use the unit--square--counit formula of [def-exchange-projection], which [fix-lem-exchanges] identifies with the actual coefficient-stage exchanges. Its transpose is
$$Lh^*P_XRh_*H\xrightarrow{c}P_YLh^*Rh_*H\xrightarrow{P_Y\varepsilon_H}P_YH.$$
On sheet $\sigma$, the square comparison $c$ is the identity after the projection identifications: both composites are pullback along $G_X$, by $hG_Ys_\sigma=G_X=G_Xhs_\sigma$, and every map involved, namely $c$, the sheet identifications $s_\sigma^*Lh^*\simeq\operatorname{id}$ of [lem-zl-split-sheet-adjunction] and those of Step 2, is a composite of the composition isomorphisms $c_{-,-}$. The associativity identity of [lem-pod-integral-pullback-composition] for the triples $(s_\sigma,h,G_X)$ and $(s_\sigma,G_Y,h)$ identifies both resulting maps $s_\sigma^*Lh^*P_X\to P_X$ with the composition isomorphism for $G_X=G_Xhs_\sigma=hG_Ys_\sigma$; it passes to the rational and common stage because those maps are rationalizations of the integral ones at one finite stage. The second arrow on this sheet is $P_X(\operatorname{pr}_{\pi(\sigma)})$. The Hom bijection of [lem-zl-split-sheet-adjunction] therefore gives the exact component equation
$$\operatorname{pr}_\sigma e_H=P_X(\operatorname{pr}_{\pi(\sigma)}).$$
These projections determine a unique morphism into the product. Replacing $\pi$ by $\pi^{-1}$ gives its inverse. This proves the claimed normalization for the actual exchange as a morphism in the derived category.

source.place: Paragraph 5: expand “commute with Frobenius” by the canonical adjunction-mate exchange

proof.text:
Apply the operation-lift formula of [lem-pod-semilinear-field-operation-lifts] to $Lh^*$ and $Rh_*$. The pullback Weil map on $Lh^*M$ has component $\theta:P_XM\to M$ on every sheet: its square comparison is the pullback-composition identity computed in Step 3. The direct-image Weil map is
$$\theta_P=Rh_*(\theta_{Lh^*M})\,e_{Lh^*M}.$$
Using the natural product description of [lem-zl-split-sheet-adjunction] and Step 3, its $\sigma$-component is exactly $\theta\,P_X(\operatorname{pr}_{\pi(\sigma)})$. This is the formula $\theta_P((v_\tau)_\tau)=(\theta(v_{\pi(\sigma)}))_\sigma$. The equalities are component equations of derived morphisms, hence also of heart morphisms; no stalk-detection assertion is being substituted for them.

source.place: Paragraph 5: combine the componentwise Weil map with the permutation exchange

proof.text: All these identifications respect finite extension of the coefficient field. Indeed [lem-zl-split-sheet-adjunction] identifies the actual adjunction and its component maps compatibly with coefficient extension; [lem-pur-finite-clopen-derived-decomposition] supplies the coefficient-compatible derived clopen equivalence. By clause (1) of [fix-lem-exchanges], the exchange respects coefficient comparisons on their stated domains. Here those domains consist only of finite clopen products, identity transports and scheme-automorphism pullbacks, so bounded constructibility and the heart are preserved in the displayed coordinates. The pullback-composition isomorphisms used for the sheet identifications in Steps 2 and 3 commute with the integral scalar-extension comparisons by clause 1 of [lem-pod-pullback-identities-scalar-extension], so these identifications are the same after passing to a larger finite coefficient field. Applying a coefficient-extension functor to $\operatorname{pr}_\sigma e_H=P_X(\operatorname{pr}_{\pi(\sigma)})$ gives the same equation with the new coefficients. The uniqueness from the product property identifies it with the new exchange. Rationalization and common-stage passage are already part of these cited identifications; no Frobenius-stable integral lattice is assumed and no rational object is reduced modulo a uniformizer.

source.place: Paragraph 5: coefficient-compatible derived, rather than only stalkwise, Frobenius comparison

proof.text:
The unit is the diagonal $\Delta:M\to\bigoplus_\sigma M$ by [lem-zl-split-sheet-adjunction]. Its Weil equation is immediate componentwise:
$$\operatorname{pr}_\sigma\theta_P P_X\Delta=\theta=\operatorname{pr}_\sigma\Delta\theta.$$
Thus it is equivariant by the morphism equation of [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]. For $m=1$ the permutation is the identity and the formula is $\theta$; for $M=0$ or $X=\varnothing$ all maps are the unique zero maps. The argument uses only finite clopen coordinates and the given Weil isomorphism, so needs no lissity, connectedness or semisimplicity.

source.place: Paragraph 5: equivariant diagonal, including the degenerate cases
